newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pork exports more than double by 2000 - group.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pork exports more than double by 2000 - group.

text.p: The U.S. Meat Export Federation estimated U.S. pork and pork variety meat exports would more than double by the year 2000 from current levels.
In a speech for delivery on Tuesday at the U.S. Agriculture Department's Agricultural Outlook Forum, the group also forecast a steady gain in U.S. beef exports through 2000.
U.S. pork exports were forecast at 415,000 tonnes in 1996; 523,000 tonnes in 1997; 653,000 tonnes in 1998; 802,000 tonnes in 1999 and 1.0 billion tonnes in 2000.
The export group estimated demand for U.S. pork from top customers Japan, Mexico, Hong Kong, China, Russia, and Korea would continue to increase between 1996-2000.
U.S. beef exports were estimated at 982,000 tonnes in 1996; 1.2 billion tonnes in 1997; 1.3 billion tonnes in 1998; 1.5 billion tonnes in 1999 and 1.7 billion tonnes in 2000.
Japan, Canada, Mexico, Korea and Russia were all seen having rising demand for U.S. beef between 1996-2000.
